input.summary: One verified finding, one delete-only fix. The orientation paragraph of the detailed description asserted that the frame's central axis "in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped" — an affirmative coaxiality relationship the inventor never discloses, and a FIG-1 depiction convention that had escaped into the application text. I deleted the untraced clause and left the sentence functioning as the naming convention for inward/outward/radial/circumferential. No substitute statement about centering, concentricity, or any other pipe/frame axis relationship was added anywhere. Nothing else changed: the claims never recited coaxiality (claim 1 recites a frame surrounding a central axis; claim 11 recites a pipe without a coaxiality limitation), so no claim support is affected, and the numeral table, drawing descriptions, abstract, and all five figure briefs stay byte for byte as approved — including FIG-1's "concentric with the pipe circle" instruction, which remains a figure-level depiction convention. No prior-art search was run for this application; the art in prior_art/ is whatever was supplied and may be incomplete, so the Background's prior-art characterizations rest on an incomplete record.

No other file changed. Claims, numeral table, drawing descriptions, abstract, summary, background, and all five figure briefs are untouched; FIG-1's concentric depiction stays confined to the brief.

content.text: I applied the three labeling corrections named in the gate report, and nothing else — no geometry bullets, numerals, or application text were touched.

input.summary: The gate report raised one verified finding: the "shown schematically" designation was applied inconsistently across FIGS. 1, 2 and 5, leaving the jaw carriage outline (and, in FIG. 2, the slideway and jaw pad) standing as an unqualified assertion of appearance that the disclosure does not support. The disclosure gives the carriage's function only ("Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad"), so the rectangle-and-parallel-lines depiction is a permissible convention that must be designated as such wherever it appears. I edited only the closing schematic-designation sentence of each of the three briefs, using the exact replacement text the report specified. No geometry bullet, numeral placement target, "Numerals shown" list, claim, description, numeral table or drawing description was altered, so the drawing pipeline will re-render and re-inspect FIGS. 1, 2 and 5 from briefs whose geometry is byte-identical to what was already approved. Note, as the drafting brief requires: no prior-art search was run for this application, and the art supplied in prior_art/ may be incomplete.
changes: figures/FIG-1.md: added the carriage blocks to the sentence designating parts shown schematically, so the carriage outline is labeled a depiction convention as it is in FIG. 5.
figures/FIG-2.md: added the slideways, the carriages and the pads to the sentence designating parts shown schematically, matching the designation those same parts already carry in FIGS. 1 and 5.
figures/FIG-5.md: added the carriage to the sentence designating parts shown schematically, so the frame portion, carriage, pad, follower, slot and spring are all designated.

No change to draft/09-claims.md, draft/08-detailed-description.md, draft/07-drawings.md, draft/numerals.md or any other application text; no geometry, numeral or embodiment was added or removed anywhere.

patches.replace: The hinge, the latch, the carriage blocks, the small blocks at the inner ends of the carriage blocks, and the mounting boss are shown schematically.
patches.why: Gate finding: the carriage block outline is a depiction convention not fixed by the disclosure, but FIG. 1 designated only the hinge, latch, pads and boss as schematic. Adding the carriage blocks makes the designation consistent with FIG. 5 without changing any geometry.

14	- Between the two boundary circles, a narrow band of two concentric arcs set toward the outer boundary, divided at the left and at the right.
15	- A channel outline of two concentric arcs, one just inboard of the band and one just outboard of it, so the band sits within the channel, the channel being divided at the left and at the right in line with the radial breaks.
16	- Three slideways through the annular body at roughly equal angular intervals, one at the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, clear of both breaks, each drawn as two parallel radial lines between the boundary circles.
17	- In each slideway a carriage drawn as a radially long rectangle narrower than the slideway, passing through the inner circle, stopping short of the centre of the drawing area, and reaching the band at its outer end.
18	- On the inner end of each carriage a pad drawn as a small block with a concave inner edge, joined to the carriage at a small circle.
19	- At the outer end of each carriage a small follower circle lying on the band, and around it a slot drawn as an elongated closed outline through the band, inclined so its long direction is neither purely radial nor purely along the band. The slots share one rotational sense.
20	- In each slideway a spring drawn as a short zigzag line acting between the carriage and the frame, so that it biases the carriage outward.
21	- A small rectangular projection standing radially outward on the outer boundary circle at the upper right, radially outboard of the channel.

input.summary: The review listed one blocker: the FIG. 2 brief was 2806 characters against a 2800 maximum. I resolved it by tightening wording in figures/FIG-2.md alone, with no loss of disclosed structure, relationships, numerals, or placement targets. Four edits: collapsed repeated definite articles in the "shown schematically" sentence, shortened "the channel being divided" to "the channel divided", shortened "Part names here are semantic identifiers only" to "Part names are semantic identifiers only", and deleted the sentence "Details of the jaw carriages are shown in FIG. 5." That last sentence was a cross-reference addressed to a reader rather than geometry for the renderer, so removing it costs the sheet nothing; the equivalent cross-reference in the Brief Description of the Drawings is untouched. The file is now 2781 characters as stored, which is under the limit whether the gate counts the whole file or the body after front matter, so it will not sit on the threshold again. No text section, claim, abstract, or numeral was changed. I confirmed FIG. 2 still lists 22, 24, 30, 36 and 66, that each has both geometry and a placement target in the brief, that each matches its single canonical part name in draft/numerals.md, and that the two specification passages mentioning FIG. 2 name only parts the sheet still carries. A sweep of draft/ and figures/ for unfinished markers and em dashes returned nothing. I disagreed with no finding.
reasoning: The only failing gate was a character count on one drawing brief, so the correct repair is a wording trim, not a re-specification of the sheet. Re-describing the geometry would risk changing what the renderer draws and would invite new numeral or visibility defects for no benefit.

I chose cuts that remove no geometry: article repetition in the schematic-parts list, a participle in the channel sentence, and one adverb. These change only prose length, so the rendered sheet is unaffected.

I removed 'Details of the jaw carriages are shown in FIG. 5' because a figure brief is a specification of geometry for one sheet; a pointer to another sheet is aimed at a reader and gives the image pipeline nothing to draw. The cross-reference that the examiner actually needs lives in the Brief Description of the Drawings, which I left alone.

I deliberately kept 'at roughly equal angular intervals' for the three slideways even though cutting it would have saved more characters, because the equal angular spacing of the three jaws is disclosure-grounded geometry that does real work in the invention, and length pressure is not a reason to drop substantive structure from a brief.

I trimmed past the minimum needed (45 characters would have cleared the gate under the reviewer's metric; I cut 95) because the reviewer's reported 2806 differs from the stored file length, meaning the gate strips some leading material. Landing under 2800 on the stored length makes the result correct under either measure rather than dependent on my inference about the metric.

I did not touch the claims, description, background, or numerals table. The review raised nothing against them, and rewriting sound text to look responsive would destroy prior work and make the change record useless.

structured_output.summary: The review listed one blocker: the FIG. 2 brief was 2806 characters against a 2800 maximum. I resolved it by tightening wording in figures/FIG-2.md alone, with no loss of disclosed structure, relationships, numerals, or placement targets. Four edits: collapsed repeated definite articles in the "shown schematically" sentence, shortened "the channel being divided" to "the channel divided", shortened "Part names here are semantic identifiers only" to "Part names are semantic identifiers only", and deleted the sentence "Details of the jaw carriages are shown in FIG. 5." That last sentence was a cross-reference addressed to a reader rather than geometry for the renderer, so removing it costs the sheet nothing; the equivalent cross-reference in the Brief Description of the Drawings is untouched. The file is now 2781 characters as stored, which is under the limit whether the gate counts the whole file or the body after front matter, so it will not sit on the threshold again. No text section, claim, abstract, or numeral was changed. I confirmed FIG. 2 still lists 22, 24, 30, 36 and 66, that each has both geometry and a placement target in the brief, that each matches its single canonical part name in draft/numerals.md, and that the two specification passages mentioning FIG. 2 name only parts the sheet still carries. A sweep of draft/ and figures/ for unfinished markers and em dashes returned nothing. I disagreed with no finding.
reasoning: The only failing gate was a character count on one drawing brief, so the correct repair is a wording trim, not a re-specification of the sheet. Re-describing the geometry would risk changing what the renderer draws and would invite new numeral or visibility defects for no benefit.

I chose cuts that remove no geometry: article repetition in the schematic-parts list, a participle in the channel sentence, and one adverb. These change only prose length, so the rendered sheet is unaffected.

I removed 'Details of the jaw carriages are shown in FIG. 5' because a figure brief is a specification of geometry for one sheet; a pointer to another sheet is aimed at a reader and gives the image pipeline nothing to draw. The cross-reference that the examiner actually needs lives in the Brief Description of the Drawings, which I left alone.

I deliberately kept 'at roughly equal angular intervals' for the three slideways even though cutting it would have saved more characters, because the equal angular spacing of the three jaws is disclosure-grounded geometry that does real work in the invention, and length pressure is not a reason to drop substantive structure from a brief.

I trimmed past the minimum needed (45 characters would have cleared the gate under the reviewer's metric; I cut 95) because the reviewer's reported 2806 differs from the stored file length, meaning the gate strips some leading material. Landing under 2800 on the stored length makes the result correct under either measure rather than dependent on my inference about the metric.

I did not touch the claims, description, background, or numerals table. The review raised nothing against them, and rewriting sound text to look responsive would destroy prior work and make the change record useless.
